findings.issue_text: **C1. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:118-120` — unguarded array access crashes Google Meet bookings without a destination calendar**

When `destinationCalendar` is `null`/`[]`, the destructure yields `undefined` and `.integration` throws `TypeError`. The old expression had optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`); it was dropped. TypeScript can't catch this (array element destructuring types as non-optional without `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`). The `&&` only reaches the right operand when location *is* Google Meet — exactly the "Meet without a Google Cal" case this branch exists for. `handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067` sets `null` when neither event type nor organizer has a DC; `confirm.handler.ts:175-179` sets `[]`. Result: 500 on every such booking instead of the Cal Video fallback.
**C2. `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151-153` — unrelated change inverts organization slug logic**
...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }),
**C3. `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256` and `:315-317` — self-referential fallback is dead code**
**I1. `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147-168` — legacy destinations silently retarget to `primary`; hangout-link patch can reject unhandled**

(a) `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable and `EventManager.ts:374-383` still calls `createEvent(c, event)` without an externalId for those; `find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` matches nothing → `"primary"` (line 154). Previously the destination was honoured unconditionally. A user whose DC row predates the `credentialId` column now gets events in their primary calendar, silently. (b) The follow-up `events.patch` at line 168 uses raw `selectedCalendar` with **no `|| "primary"` and no `.catch`** → unhandled rejection on every Meet booking that took the fallback (process-terminating under Node ≥15 defaults; at best the description never gets the hangout link). (c) Matching by `credentialId` is ambiguous — one credential can own several destination calendars, so two iterations can both resolve to the same calendar (duplicate in one, missing in the other).
*Fix:* thread the already-known `externalId` from `CalendarManager.createEvent` (`CalendarManager.ts:221`) into the service, use one variable for both `insert` and `patch`, and add `.catch`.
**I2. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:170` — video references lose `credentialId`**
credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId,

Only the calendar branch needed changing; the video branch now hardcodes `undefined`. `handleCancelBooking.ts:488-497` requires `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` before `deleteMeeting`, and `deleteCredential.handler.ts` matches bookings by it. Failure: user with two Zoom accounts cancels → guard fails → Zoom meeting never deleted.
**I3. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:201-209` (`updateLocation`) — recreated references have null `externalCalendarId` *and* `credentialId`**

Those results come from `CalendarManager.updateEvent` (`CalendarManager.ts:312-322`), whose return object sets neither field, so both are always `undefined`. `editLocation.handler.ts:116-119` writes them straight back via `references: { create: … }`. Previously the `evt.destinationCalendar` fallbacks filled them. Failure: edit a booking's location → new references are degraded → later cancel takes the legacy all-credentials branch and, via C3, deletes from `primary`.

`office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73-77`, `larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128-129`, and `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-165` (CalDAV/Apple base) keep using `destinationCalendar[0]`, while `createAllCalendarEvents` now calls them once per destination *with a different credential each time*. Collective event with two Office 365 hosts: iteration 2 uses host B's credential against host A's calendar URL → 403/404, host B gets no event, yet the stored reference records host B's `externalId` (`CalendarManager.ts:267`). For CalDAV the filter matches zero calendars and `Promise.all([])` resolves silently. Net regression versus previous single-event behavior for these providers.
**I5. `handleCancelBooking.ts:443-470` — recurring-cancel block moved inside the per-reference loop**
**I6. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:592` — error message built then discarded**
**I7. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:540` — possibly-`undefined` credential passed to `updateEvent`**

If the DB lookup at `:516-538` returns nothing (or no `app.slug`), `credential` stays `undefined` and `updateEvent` dereferences `credential.appName` (`CalendarManager.ts:314`) → `TypeError`. `credential` is an untyped `let` (`:480`) so TS doesn't flag it. The throw escapes the whole loop, so one missing credential fails the update for all hosts — silently, per I6.
**I8. `handleNewBooking.ts:1077-1079` — co-host calendars silently dropped**

**I9. Silent skips leave the booking looking successful** (`EventManager.ts:356-372`) — a destination whose credential can't be resolved is skipped with no log and no `EventResult`, so `handleNewBooking` sees success. With N hosts this is N times more likely than before. Push a `success: false` result instead.

**I10. No test coverage for the new behavior.** The only test touched is a fixture literal (`apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249`). Nothing exercises two destinations → two `createEvent` calls, the DB hydration fallback, the per-reference update/cancel loops, `credentialId: null` destinations, or the empty-`destinationCalendar` path that C1 crashes on. The private methods are reachable via `EventManager.create/update` with a mocked prisma and fake `Calendar`.

**I11. Breaking public payload/API change, undocumented.** `destinationCalendar` object → array is breaking for webhook consumers (hence the e2e fixture edit) and for any `Calendar` implementation outside this diff. Also `Calendar.createEvent` (`packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221`) gained a **required** `credentialId: number` param, breaking out-of-tree callers — make it optional and grep the full monorepo before merge.

**I12. Performance: serialized creates and N+1 queries on the booking hot path** — `EventManager.ts:339-382` awaits each destination sequentially and issues one `findUnique` per uncached destination (same at `:516-538` and `handleCancelBooking.ts:432-440`). Batch with `findMany({ id: { in: … } })` and `Promise.all` the independent creates.

**DRY:** the ~20-line credential-hydration block is copy-pasted at `EventManager.ts:342-368` and `:516-538` (identical, including a redundant `?? ""` after the `&&` guard), plus a variant in `handleCancelBooking.ts:432-440`. Extract a helper.

**`handleNewBooking.ts:724-762` (`loadUsers` rewrite, out of scope):** dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic select while `IsFixedAwareUser` (`:355`) still declares it and `users` is force-cast at `:869` — the type now lies. Also the new `catch` maps `new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` to **500** because `instanceof HttpError` fails for a plain `Error`; that's a 400.

**`handleNewBooking.ts:689`:** `["COLLECTIVE","ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(...)` and string-literal `"COLLECTIVE"` comparisons at `:992`/`:1077` lose enum safety while `SchedulingType` is still used at `:805` — inconsistent within one file.
**No dedupe of destination calendars** (`:992-993`): two co-hosts sharing a calendar → two identical events.

**Inconsistent empty representation:** `null` at `handleNewBooking.ts:1067` vs `[]` everywhere else (`handleCancelBooking.ts:251-255`, `confirm.handler.ts:175-179`, `webhook.ts:119`). Standardize on `[]`.

**`googlecalendar:122-123, 228-229`:** organizer `email` still comes from the *main host's* destination even when writing into another host's calendar — mixing per-credential and main-host routing in one payload; needs a comment if deliberate.

**Hydrated co-host credentials bypass `refreshCredentials`** (`handleNewBooking.ts:1253` refreshes only the organizer's) and skip the `credential.invalid` check. Latent for Google (refreshes internally), a problem for the next provider.

**Unrelated churn** inflating the diff: `orginalBookingDuration`→`originalBookingDuration`, `"organiser"`→`"organizer"` in a user-visible calendar note (`CalendarManager.ts:230`), `import type` split in `builders/CalendarEvent/builder.ts`, `firstName`/`lastName` added at `handleNewBooking.ts:999-1000`.
**Comment grammar** `EventManager.ts:117`: "destinationCalendar it's an array now" → "is an array now".
**`EventManager.ts:159-161`:** with N calendar results, `evt.iCalUID` is overwritten by the last one — pre-existing, newly ambiguous.

**Defense in depth:** `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id } })` fetches any credential by id with no ownership scoping. Ids come from server-written rows, so not exploitable today, but `userId: { in: hostUserIds }` would make the guarantee local.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **I1. `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147-168` — legacy destinations silently retarget to `primary`; hangout-link patch can reject unhandled**

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now selects the target calendar via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId;` and then calls `calendar.events.insert` with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. If `destinationCalendar` entries exist but lack `credentialId` (or it doesn’t match the passed `credentialId`), `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` and the event is silently created in the user’s `primary` calendar. Previously the code would use `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.externalId` directly (no credentialId matching), so this diff introduces a behavioral regression for such “legacy”/mismatched destinationCalendar data. The second clause about a "hangout-link patch" isn’t clearly supported by the shown diff, but the silent fallback-to-primary retargeting is verifiable here.

Previously the destination was honoured unconditionally. A user whose DC row predates the `credentialId` column now gets events in their primary calendar, silently. (b) The follow-up `events.patch` at line 168 uses raw `selectedCalendar` with **no `|| "primary"` and no `.catch`** → unhandled rejection on every Meet booking that took the fallback (process-terminating under Node ≥15 defaults; at best the description never gets the hangout link). (c) Matching by `credentialId` is ambiguous — one credential can own several destination calendars, so two iterations can both resolve to the same calendar (duplicate in one, missing in the other).
*Fix:* thread the already-known `externalId` from `CalendarManager.createEvent` (`CalendarManager.ts:221`) into the service, use one variable for both `insert` and `patch`, and add `.catch`.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` the mapping that builds reference objects was changed from `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. This means when `isCalendarType` is false (i.e., video/dedicated integrations), the reference no longer records `result.credentialId` and will always have `credentialId` as `undefined`, which is a concrete loss of data compared to the prior behavior.

**I5. `handleCancelBooking.ts:443-470` — recurring-cancel block moved inside the per-reference loop**

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In the new code `bookingCalendarReference` is changed from a single `.find(...)` result to an array via `.filter(...)`, and the recurring-cancel deletion logic (the `if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && ... ) { const promises = bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).map(...) ... await Promise.all(promises) }` block) now runs inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Since that recurring block already iterates over *all* calendar credentials and all `updatedBookings`, placing it inside the per-reference loop will repeat the same deletion work once per calendar reference, causing duplicate delete attempts / extra API calls and potential failures or rate-limit issues.

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.updateBookingEvent (around the changed block starting ~476), `credential` is declared as an untyped `let` (`..., credential;`). Inside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop, when `reference.credentialId` is present, the code attempts to resolve `credential` from `this.calendarCredentials`, otherwise it does a DB lookup and only assigns `credential` if `credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug`. If the DB lookup returns null OR returns a row without `app.slug`, `credential` remains `undefined`, but the code still executes `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));` with no guard. That is a concrete runtime bug: `updateEvent` (and the downstream calendar manager logic) expects a credential object and is very likely to dereference properties like `credential.appName`/`credential.id`, causing a `TypeError`. Because this happens inside the try, a thrown error will jump to the catch and return failure results for all references, so one missing/invalid credential can break updates for all hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Defense in depth:** `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id } })` fetches any credential by id with no ownership scoping. Ids come from server-written rows, so not exploitable today, but `userId: { in: hostUserIds }` would make the guarantee local.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple new `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: ... } })` fallbacks when a credential isn’t found in the in-memory `calendarCredentials`/`user.credentials` lists (e.g., in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, `EventManager.updateCalendarEvent` path, and `handleCancelBooking`). These lookups are not scoped to an expected owner (user/team/hostUserIds) and will return any credential row for that id. Since the id is taken from persisted booking data (`destination.credentialId` / `reference.credentialId`), it’s likely server-written today, but the lack of ownership constraint is a real, verifiable defense-in-depth/access-control weakness introduced by the diff (previously it only used already-associated credentials).
